finding: CRITICAL: Round 85 log-J formula was WRONG. Used (K*ln(J)/J)*C^{-1} instead of K*ln(J)*C^{-1}.
error_origin: Forgot the chain rule cancellation: S = 2*(dW/dJ)*(dJ/dC) = 2*(K*ln(J)/J)*(J/2)*C^{-1} = K*ln(J)*C^{-1}
impact: Round 85 SfePy+logJ and Round 85 analytical reference both used the wrong formula CONSISTENTLY, so they agreed (0.004% diff). But NEITHER would agree with FEBio, which uses the correct formula.
lesson: Stress equivalence between two implementations is NOT evidence of constitutive correctness. Both implementations can be wrong in the same way. The tangent-equivalence check would have caught this because the tangent of the wrong formula differs from the tangent of the correct formula.
cemetery_entry_candidate: CE-023: Two wrong implementations can agree. Consistency is not correctness. The tangent-equivalence check is needed because it forces re-derivation of the stress from first principles, which catches errors that are invisible to stress-only comparison.
